notes: English port of tests/e2e/data/it/gold_graph.json for the Carol Della Chiesa translation (Gutenberg #500). Keywords are word-start prefixes. Where the translation differs, the English text wins (g14/g30 the well of Farmer John instead of the water wheel of Giangio; g27 fifty pennies and fifty gold coins instead of forty).

questions.question: Who are all the characters who deceive Pinocchio during the story?
questions.notes: Fox and Cat (ch. 12-19: Field of Wonders, Assassins, City of Simple Simons); Lamp-Wick and the Little Man (ch. 30-31: Land of Toys, turning into a donkey).

questions.question: Which animals help Pinocchio during the story?
questions.notes: Pigeon that carries him to the sea (ch. 23), Dolphin with news of Geppetto (ch. 24), Alidoro who saves him from the fisherman (ch. 28-29), Snail (ch. 29), Tunny inside the Shark (ch. 34, 36).

questions.question: In which places is Pinocchio imprisoned or locked up during the story?
questions.notes: Prison for four months by the Gorilla judge (ch. 19); the doghouse with the chain as a watchdog (ch. 21-22); inside the Terrible Shark (ch. 34-35); the Green Fisherman's cave (ch. 28).

questions.question: What is the relationship between the Fairy with Azure Hair and the Snail?
questions.notes: The Snail is the Fairy's maid (ch. 29: opens the door and brings breakfast; ch. 36: 'the Snail that lived with the Fairy').

questions.question: Whom does Pinocchio meet inside the body of the Shark?
questions.notes: The Tunny (ch. 34) and his father Geppetto, shut in there for two years (ch. 35).

questions.question: Which characters try to burn, fry, hang or eat Pinocchio during the story?
questions.notes: Fire Eater wants to use him as firewood to roast the mutton (ch. 11); the Assassins hang him on the oak (ch. 14-15); the Green Fisherman wants to fry him (ch. 28); the Shark swallows him (ch. 34).

questions.question: What transformations does Pinocchio go through during the story?
questions.notes: Nose that grows with his lies (ch. 17); donkey ears and body (ch. 32); back to a Marionette in the sea (ch. 34); a real boy at the end (ch. 36).

questions.question: Which places does Pinocchio pass through on his journey, from the inn to the islands and countries?
questions.notes: Inn of the Red Lobster (ch. 13, 17), Field of Wonders and City of Simple Simons (ch. 18-19), Island of the Busy Bees (ch. 24), Land of Toys (ch. 30-33).

questions.question: Who gives Pinocchio advice or warnings so that he becomes a good boy?
questions.notes: The Talking Cricket (ch. 4, 13, 16, 36), the Fairy (ch. 16-17, 25, 29), Geppetto who scolds him (ch. 3) and sells his coat for the A-B-C book (ch. 8-9).

questions.question: Which animals serve the Fairy with Azure Hair?
questions.notes: The Falcon (ch. 16), the Poodle Medoro (ch. 16), the Snail maid (ch. 29, 36).

questions.question: Who saves Pinocchio from mortal danger during the story?
questions.notes: The Maiden/Fairy has him taken down from the giant oak with the Falcon and Medoro (ch. 15-16); Alidoro saves him from the Green Fisherman (ch. 28-29); the Tunny carries him and Geppetto ashore (ch. 36). Fire Eater sparing him (ch. 11) is also acceptable.

questions.question: What lies does Pinocchio tell and to whom?
questions.notes: He tells the Fairy he lost the gold pieces, then that he swallowed them: his nose grows (ch. 17). To Geppetto he says the cat ate his feet, but he burned them on the foot warmer (ch. 6-7). Lies must be presented as lies, not as facts.

questions.question: Which doctors examine Pinocchio at the Fairy's house and what do they say?
questions.notes: The Crow, the Owl and the Talking Cricket (ch. 16). Crow: he is dead, but if not dead he is alive; Owl: the opposite; the Cricket recognizes him and calls him a rascal and a disobedient son.

questions.question: What jobs does Pinocchio do to earn food or a living?
questions.notes: Watchdog for the Farmer (ch. 21-22); carries the jug for the little woman in exchange for bread (ch. 24); draws water from the well for Farmer John in exchange for milk and makes baskets of reeds (ch. 36).

questions.question: Who sells and who buys Pinocchio once he has become a donkey?
questions.notes: The Little Man takes him to the market and sells him to the owner of a circus (ch. 33); lamed, he is sold again to a man who wants his skin for a drumhead (ch. 33-34).

questions.question: Which characters die, or are believed dead, during the story?
questions.notes: The Talking Cricket killed with the hammer (ch. 4); the Maiden who says she is dead (ch. 15) and the marble stone saying she died of grief (ch. 23); the Blackbird eaten by the Cat (ch. 12); Eugene believed dead on the beach (ch. 27); Lamp-Wick the donkey who dies at Farmer John's (ch. 36); Pinocchio himself believed dead by the doctors (ch. 16).

questions.question: What happens to the boys who go to the Land of Toys, and who profits from it?
questions.notes: After five months they turn into donkeys (ch. 32); the Little Man who brought them in his coach sells them at markets and fairs and has become a millionaire (ch. 33).

questions.question: What becomes of the Fox and the Cat at the end of the book?
questions.notes: Ch. 36: reduced to misery, they beg for alms; the Cat, after pretending to be blind for years, has really lost his sight; the Fox, old, thin and almost hairless, has lost his tail (sold it for a bite to eat). Pinocchio refuses to help them.

questions.question: Who was Melampo and what deal did he have with the Weasels?
questions.notes: Melampo was the Farmer's watchdog, who died that morning (ch. 21); he let the Weasels steal the chickens in exchange for one chicken (ch. 22). Pinocchio refuses the deal, barks and gets the Weasels caught.

questions.question: What does Pinocchio eat, or what is he given to eat, when he is hungry?
questions.notes: He finds an egg from which a Chick hatches and flies away (ch. 5); Geppetto gives him three pears, and he eats the skins and cores too (ch. 7); the little woman gives him bread and cauliflower (ch. 24); the Fairy sends him fake bread of chalk, chicken of cardboard and fruit (ch. 29).

questions.question: Who is arrested or put in prison during the story, and by whom?
questions.notes: Geppetto is taken to prison by a Carabineer instead of Pinocchio (ch. 3); Pinocchio is sentenced by the Judge (a Gorilla) and taken by the Mastiffs dressed as Carabineers, four months (ch. 19); Pinocchio is arrested by the Carabineers for Eugene's wound, then escapes (ch. 27).

questions.question: What happens on the beach between Pinocchio and his schoolmates, and how does it end?
questions.notes: The boys lure him to the sea with the lie about the Shark; in the fight they throw books, an arithmetic text hits Eugene; the boys run away, the Carabineers arrive and arrest Pinocchio, who escapes chased by Alidoro (ch. 26-27).

questions.question: What is the relationship between Geppetto and Mastro Cherry, and where does Pinocchio's wood come from?
questions.notes: Old friends who quarrel and fight twice over the nickname Polendina, then make peace (ch. 2); Mastro Cherry gives Geppetto the piece of wood that talks and laughs (ch. 1-2).

questions.question: In which forms or appearances does the Fairy with Azure Hair present herself during the story?
questions.notes: Lovely Maiden at the window (ch. 15); good little woman carrying the jugs who then becomes his mother (ch. 24-25); lady in the circus box with the medallion (ch. 33); little azure Goat on the rock (ch. 34); in a dream at the end (ch. 36).

questions.question: Which animals speak to Pinocchio to warn him, scold him or explain what is happening to him?
questions.notes: Talking Cricket (ch. 4, 13); white Blackbird (ch. 12); Parrot laughing at him at the Field of Wonders (ch. 19); Glowworm (ch. 21); Crab on the beach (ch. 27); little Dormouse explaining the donkey fever (ch. 32).

questions.question: How does Geppetto end up inside the Shark and how does he survive in there?
questions.notes: He sets off in a little boat to look for Pinocchio across the ocean (ch. 23), the waves overturn the boat and the Terrible Shark swallows him; he has lived there for two years on the provisions of a swallowed ship (meat, preserved food, crackers, wine, candles), now almost gone (ch. 35).

questions.question: Who gives Pinocchio money during the story and what becomes of that money?
questions.notes: Fire Eater gives him five gold pieces for Geppetto (ch. 11-12): one goes to the innkeeper of the Red Lobster, four are stolen by the Fox and the Cat at the Field of Wonders (ch. 13, 19). At the end he saves fifty pennies for a suit and gives them to the Snail for the sick Fairy; the Fairy returns fifty gold coins (ch. 36).

questions.question: Which characters are connected to the Marionette Theater?
questions.notes: The showman Fire Eater, Harlequin and Pulcinella who recognize Pinocchio from the stage, Signora Rosaura (ch. 10-11).

questions.question: Which sea creatures appear in the story and what role do they play?
questions.notes: Dolphin with news of Geppetto (ch. 24); Crab scolding the boys (ch. 27); fish eating the donkey skin (ch. 34); Terrible Shark swallowing Geppetto and Pinocchio (ch. 34-35); Tunny, fellow prisoner who carries them ashore (ch. 34, 36).

questions.question: What is the link between Lamp-Wick and Farmer John?
questions.notes: Farmer John bought Lamp-Wick, turned into a donkey, and made him draw water; the donkey dies worn out by hunger and work in front of Pinocchio, who recognizes him (ch. 36).
